searchText: [**E2HS**(Execution Layer History) SPEC](<https://github.com/eth-clients/e2store-format-specs/blob/main/formats/e2hs.md>) - **full execution layer history** for execution clients, provides data from genesis to latest, headers are accompanied by proofs of canonicalness. Here is a link to download E2HS files <https://e2hs.ethportal.net/index.html>. I am uploading E2HS files 1898 to 2370 right now. So up to block 19415040. I should be able to upload files upto HEAD-8192 blocks, in a week, as I am waiting on a few PR's to be merged to continue generating the files. We will be setting up a script which uploads new E2HS files every 27 hours. Download links to e2store files in general can be found here <https://eth-clients.github.io/history-endpoints/> Interesting. I did not consider this. Does any client actually sync blocks backwards? regarding the sampling, it's something to investigate for later, but as we discussed, it doesn't really add a lot of security just means the 'fake clients' have to become a bit smarter in routing their requests one thing we could do is, couple the sampling with latency requirements, but it's a bit dangerous here's one from the bad ideas zone: - in the server, add logic so the 'first request' from every peer within a certain time window has a minimum latency of, say, 100ms - on the client side, when sampling history, check that response latency is < 100ms this would make it a bit harder for fake clients to use legitimate peers satisfy the sampling requests I think Nethermind and Besu do after a snap sync Need the head 256 blocks to start processing blocks; so want them first; or have to wait for every block to be downloaded to start processing if going forwards, which would be a long time after snap sync completes vs going backwards from head I see so you download backwards all the way, or just backwards a little bit to get some blocks to process? I think all the way; depends on the sync method chosen, fast-sync, full/archive sync we go forward. However snap sync is preferred as is fastest. Then backwards sync so we can start attesting fast and minimize offline time <@628018527470616606> to confirm Also a syncing node will start with a 0 range regardless; so seems a problem to disconnect on basis that it's not the full agreed range? good day Maybe if a peers range isn't improving over time would be a better heuristic? Is mostly cause to disconnect that bothers me (and does it even need to be in spec?) backwards all the way

excerpts.author: kolbyml
excerpts.content:
[**E2HS**(Execution Layer History) SPEC](<https://github.com/eth-clients/e2store-format-specs/blob/main/formats/e2hs.md>) - **full execution layer history** for execution clients, provides data from genesis to latest, headers are accompanied by proofs of canonicalness.

Here is a link to download E2HS files <https://e2hs.ethportal.net/index.html>. I am uploading E2HS files 1898 to 2370 right now. So up to block 19415040. I should be able to upload files upto HEAD-8192 blocks, in a week, as I am waiting on a few PR's to be merged to continue generating the files. We will be setting up a script which uploads new E2HS files every 27 hours.

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content:
here's one from the bad ideas zone:

- in the server, add logic so the 'first request' from every peer within a certain time window has a minimum latency of, say, 100ms
- on the client side, when sampling history, check that response latency is < 100ms

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: this would make it a bit harder for fake clients to use legitimate peers satisfy the sampling requests

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content: Need the head 256 blocks to start processing blocks; so want them first; or have to wait for every block to be downloaded to start processing if going forwards, which would be a long time after snap sync completes vs going backwards from head

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: so you download backwards all the way, or just backwards a little bit to get some blocks to process?

excerpts.author: ben_a_adams
excerpts.content:
I think all the way; depends on the sync method chosen, fast-sync, full/archive sync we go forward. However snap sync is preferred as is fastest. Then backwards sync so we can start attesting fast and minimize offline time
